record.title: Rosetta paper reports autonomous first-principles performance models that surface assumptions in architecture papers
record.summary: The arXiv v1 paper describes Rosetta, a multi-agent pipeline that turns architecture-paper PDFs into a mathematical specification, executable Python model and plain-English interpretation. In 12 expert-reviewed papers, evaluators rated specification and interpretation quality 4 or 5 out of 5 for 10 papers and reported no significant hallucinations. A six-group author self-evaluation reported concrete paper changes in four cases. The paper also reports a broader 97-paper benchmark result, but its abstract, results section and conclusion give inconsistent denominators and percentages; that result is not summarized as settled.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors describe Rosetta as an autonomous multi-agent pipeline that converts a research-paper PDF into a mathematical specification, executable Python model and plain-English interpretation, using first-principles derivation, separate functional/scientific verification and a three-run selector.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For 12 selected architecture papers assessed by independent researchers, the paper reports specification-plus-interpretation scores of at least 4/5 on 10 papers and zero significant hallucinations; it also reports model scores from 2/5 to 5/5, including named specification or baseline failures.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In a six-group author self-evaluation, the paper reports that Rosetta output led to revisions or new experiments in four active submissions and five evaluators said they would use it again.

claims.label: DISPUTED
claims.text: The paper gives inconsistent CS2 breadth-study denominators and rates: the abstract reports 56% of fit-screened papers and says 97 papers were scored; Section VI reports 60% of 97 unfiltered papers; the conclusion reports 56% across 78. The aggregate rate and denominator are unresolved within v1.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish independent reproduction, transfer to other frontier models, or dependable numerical correctness across architecture papers beyond its reported studies.

evidence_gaps.description: The author-reported evaluations and generated performance models were not independently reproduced.
The v1 abstract, breadth-study results and conclusion disagree on the CS2 denominator and Tier-A percentage (97 / 60% versus 78 / 56%, with another fit-screened 56% formulation).
All experiments use Claude Opus 4.5; portability to newer or different model families is not evaluated.

brief.importance_rationale: If reproducible, autonomous first-principles models could make architecture claims easier to inspect and help researchers find assumptions or missing parameters, affecting hardware research practice. The reported evidence is preliminary and does not establish broad adoption or reliable numerical validation.
limitations: Single arXiv v1 preprint; no independent reproduction was conducted.
The 12-paper CS1 study uses human evaluators, but the paper reports that expertise was broad rather than deeply specialized and that evaluator scores vary by paper.
Model quality ranges from 2/5 to 5/5; the paper describes an incorrect baseline model and a model faithfully carrying forward a flawed specification.
The six-group CS3 results are a small author self-evaluation.
The experiments use Claude Opus 4.5 and do not establish cross-model transfer.
The CS2 breadth-study denominator and rate conflict between abstract, main text and conclusion.
brief.summary: The arXiv v1 paper describes Rosetta, a multi-agent pipeline that turns architecture-paper PDFs into a mathematical specification, executable Python model and plain-English interpretation. In 12 expert-reviewed papers, evaluators rated specification and interpretation quality 4 or 5 out of 5 for 10 papers and reported no significant hallucinations. A six-group author self-evaluation reported concrete paper changes in four cases. The paper also reports a broader 97-paper benchmark result, but its abstract, results section and conclusion give inconsistent denominators and percentages; that result is not summarized as settled.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report expert-rated 4–5/5 specification-plus-interpretation quality on 10 of 12 papers and four instances of concrete paper changes among six author-evaluators. Their separate 97-paper breadth result has unresolved internal denominator/rate inconsistencies and is not treated as a stable aggregate.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper reports a median end-to-end wall-clock time of 72 minutes, reducible to about 25 minutes with parallel ensemble runs. Token/API cost and expert review cost are not established here.
technical.demonstrated_result: Direct inspection confirms the arXiv v1 preprint contains the described method, evaluation protocols, results and internal inconsistencies. The empirical performance and usability claims remain author-reported.
technical.implementation_status: The paper states that code, prompts and evaluation artifacts are released with the preprint; this activation inspected the paper text but not the linked repository.
technical.mechanism: A multi-agent workflow generates a mathematical specification from a paper, implements an executable model, then explains its implications. The authors describe a shared first-principles constitution, separate functional and scientific checks, repair loops, and best-of-three selection.
technical.regime: The preprint reports 12 expert-reviewed ISCA/ASPLOS/MICRO papers, 97 ISCA 2025 and HPCA 2026 papers in a broader study, and six active research groups. Experiments use Claude Opus 4.5; reported pipeline execution is autonomous.
technical.reproducibility: The paper describes released code and evaluation artifacts, but they were not inspected or run in this activation. Independent reproduction remains open.
technical.strongest_baseline: Human evaluation of generated artifacts against source papers and paper claims; no matched competing model-generation system or independent replication is reported.

brief.title: Rosetta paper reports autonomous first-principles performance models that surface assumptions in architecture papers
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported method holds up, automatically deriving auditable performance models could reduce the expert effort needed to inspect hardware claims and expose missing assumptions. The current evidence is one preprint, with small human-evaluation samples, disclosed model-quality failures and inconsistent aggregate benchmark figures.
